intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through ancient Khmer temples including Bayon and Ta Prohm. Book a tuk-tuk driver based near Siem Reap's Old Market area for easy access. Given late flight arrival on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 morning when you are well-rested. Stay in a hotel within 3km of Angkor Wat to minimize travel time.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace & Silver Pagoda
experiences.description: Visit the stunning Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda in the heart of Phnom Penh, showcasing Khmer architecture and royal heritage. Choose a hotel in the Riverside or BKK1 district to walk or take a short tuk-tuk ride. Ideal for a mid-trip cultural day after settling in from Siem Reap.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Day
experiences.description: Take a ferry from Sihanoukville to the pristine Saracen Bay on Koh Rong Samloem for crystal-clear waters and white sand beaches. Stay overnight on the island to maximize beach time and avoid wasting a day on transit. Book accommodation directly on the island near the pier for convenience.

experiences.name: Khmer Cooking Class in Siem Reap
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class near the Old Market area, learning to prepare traditional dishes like Fish Amok and Lok Lak. Classes typically include a local market tour in the morning. Staying near Pub Street or the Old Market ensures you can walk to the class, making it easy to fit in on Day 2 afternoon after the Angkor morning visit.
experiences.location: Old Market Area (Phsar Chas), Siem Reap

experiences.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum & Killing Fields Tour
experiences.description: A deeply moving and essential historical experience visiting the S-21 prison museum and Choeung Ek Killing Fields memorial. Both sites are located in or near Phnom Penh city center. Stay in the BKK1 or Riverside district to access these sites easily by tuk-tuk within 15–30 minutes, avoiding long cross-city transfers.
experiences.location: Toul Sleng & Choeung Ek, Phnom Penh

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Siem Reap Boutique Stay, freshen up, then take a leisurely walk through the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area to get oriented. Browse local stalls, pick up a SIM card, and exchange currency at a local money changer for the best rates.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the surrounding alleys to soak up the lively atmosphere. Explore the Night Market near the river for affordable souvenirs and local snacks. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: N/A — arriving at 13:00; grab a quick snack at the airport or a street food stall near the hotel ($1–2)
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Old Market — try amok fish curry and rice for around $4–6 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Buy a local SIM card at the airport (~$3–5) for maps and communication. November is the tail end of rainy season — carry a light rain jacket just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at Angkor Wat — arrive by 5:30 AM to witness the iconic sunrise over the temple's reflection pool. Explore the main temple complex, admiring the bas-reliefs depicting Hindu mythology and the five iconic towers. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) for best value across multiple days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom complex — explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, then walk through the Baphuon, Elephant Terrace, and Terrace of the Leper King. Take a shaded rest break and hydrate frequently.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit the Angkor National Museum on your own time or simply relax. Head to the vibrant Night Market for dinner and a traditional Apsara dance performance (free outdoor previews available near the market).

meals.breakfast: Grab a $1 baguette with egg (French-influenced Khmer breakfast) from a street vendor near the hotel before heading out
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at one of the basic local restaurants just outside the Angkor complex entrance (~$3–4 for rice and grilled chicken)
meals.dinner: Genevieve's Restaurant or a local Khmer eatery near Pub Street — $4–6 for a full meal with local beer (~$1)

day_by_day.notes: Rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) or hire a tuk-tuk for the day ($12–15) to navigate Angkor. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 2 liters of water. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees must be covered at temple sites.

day_by_day.morning: Use Day 2 of the Angkor Pass to visit Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'Tomb Raider' temple dramatically overgrown with giant tree roots. Then head to Banteay Kdei and the peaceful Srah Srang reservoir, perfect for quiet reflection and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pre Rup and East Mebon temples, which are less crowded and offer a more authentic exploration experience. Alternatively, rent a bicycle and take the quieter jungle paths between temples for a budget-friendly adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry) to see silk weaving and stone carving demonstrations supporting local artisans. Browse their gallery before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Coconut porridge or rice soup (borbor) from a local market stall — $1–2
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local bakery or a simple $2–3 rice dish from a vendor near the temple complex
meals.dinner: Mahob Restaurant — authentic Khmer cuisine in a cultural setting, mains around $5–7

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm gets crowded mid-morning; arrive early. Bicycle rental is ideal today as the temples are relatively close together on the small circuit route.

day_by_day.morning: Day 3 of the Angkor Pass — venture to the outer temples. Start with Banteay Srei, the 'Citadel of Women,' known for its exquisitely detailed pink sandstone carvings. This is considered one of the finest examples of Khmer art and is about 25 km from Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Landmine Museum (free/donation) on the way back — a sobering and important cultural and historical site that tells Cambodia's painful modern history. Then visit Banteay Samre temple, a hidden gem rarely visited by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset at Phnom Bakheng hill temple (requires a timed ticket, free with Angkor Pass — book early). Watch the sun set over the jungle canopy and distant Angkor Wat silhouette.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a $1.50 fried rice with egg from a nearby stall
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in the Banteay Srei village area — $3–4 for Khmer noodle soup or lok lak (stir-fried beef with rice)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Old Market — try grilled skewers, fresh spring rolls, and fruit shakes for under $5 total

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk for the day ($15–18) as Banteay Srei is far. Book the Phnom Bakheng sunset ticket early in the morning at the Angkor ticket office — slots fill up fast. This is your last day using the 3-day pass.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonle Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Visit the floating villages of Kampong Phluk (dry season accessible) or Chong Kneas to witness the unique stilted and floating community lifestyle. A shared boat tour costs around $10–15.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Wat Preah Prom Rath temple in the city center — a beautifully maintained active pagoda that's free to enter. Explore the surrounding neighborhood on foot and interact with friendly locals.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost traditional Khmer shadow puppet show (Sbek Thom) — check local community boards or ask your hotel for current shows. Explore the Siem Reap River walk at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Num Banh Chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry sauce) from a morning market — $1–1.50, a beloved local breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat trip or eat at a floating village restaurant (~$3–4)
meals.dinner: Romdeng or a similar social enterprise restaurant — delicious Khmer food while supporting local communities, mains $5–8

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate boat prices before boarding at Chong Kneas. Kampong Phluk is more authentic but requires a tuk-tuk ride plus boat. November water levels are still relatively high, making navigation easier.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours). Book with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for a comfortable, safe, and affordable ride (~$9–12). Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh around 1:00–2:00 PM. Check in to a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area (~$8–15/night). Head to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex — a stunning example of Khmer royal architecture with gleaming spires and sacred Buddha statues ($10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay (Phnom Penh Riverside) as the sun sets over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Browse the evening market stalls and enjoy the cool river breeze.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near the Siem Reap bus station before departure — rice porridge or a baguette sandwich ($1–2)
meals.lunch: Snacks on the bus or a quick stop at a roadside restaurant during the journey ($2–3)
meals.dinner: Riverside food stalls or Friends the Restaurant (social enterprise) near the waterfront — $4–7 per meal

day_by_day.notes: Book the bus ticket a day in advance to secure a seat. Store valuables securely during the bus journey. Phnom Penh is busier and more urban than Siem Reap — stay alert in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically essential site documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities of the 1970s. Entry is $5. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit with the audio guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (~15 km from city center, $3–5 tuk-tuk ride). The $6 entry includes an excellent audio guide. This is a profoundly important historical site — pay respects at the memorial stupa.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and decompress with a peaceful walk through Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name. Visit at dusk when the atmosphere is calm. Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) area for evening street food.

meals.breakfast: Local Khmer breakfast at a nearby market — fried dough sticks (chakquai) with condensed milk coffee ($1–2)
meals.lunch: Simple rice and curry at a local canteen near Tuol Sleng (~$2–3)
meals.dinner: Street food near the Central Market — Khmer BBQ (grilled meats and vegetables at your table) for ~$5–7 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy — take your time and be respectful. These are essential for understanding Cambodia's modern history. Avoid scheduling fun activities immediately after.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early bus or shared minivan from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours, ~$7–10). Alternatively, travel to Kampot (~3 hours, ~$7) for a more relaxed coastal base. Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM. Kampot is recommended for budget travelers seeking culture + beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot. Check in to a riverside guesthouse or hostel (~$6–12/night). Rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) and explore the charming French colonial town center — admire the faded colonial architecture, pepper plantations, and the Kampot River.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the Kampot riverside promenade — one of the most beautiful and underrated sunsets in Cambodia. The sky turns golden over the Elephant Mountains.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before the bus departs — bánh mì sandwich or rice dish ($1–2)
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus or eat at a roadside stop ($2–3)
meals.dinner: Epic Arts Café or a riverside restaurant in Kampot — fresh Kampot pepper crab (a local specialty) or grilled fish with rice (~$5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is a hidden gem — quieter, cheaper, and more culturally rich than Sihanoukville. November may bring occasional light rain but the weather is generally pleasant. Kampot pepper is world-famous — try it in everything!

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike (~$7–10/day) or join a cheap group tour to Kep — a sleepy seaside town 25 km from Kampot. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market on the beach and watch fishermen bring in their morning catch. Walk through the overgrown ruins of Kep's French colonial villas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim and relax at Kep Beach or take a short boat ride to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a pristine, undeveloped island with white sand beaches and clear water ($5 return boat trip). Snorkel, swim, or simply relax in a hammock under the palm trees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot by sunset. Visit a Kampot pepper farm on the outskirts of town (many offer free or low-cost tours) to learn about Cambodia's prized export. Enjoy a final evening along the river.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and coffee at a Kampot riverside café — $2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh steamed crab with Kampot pepper sauce at the Kep Crab Market — $5–8 for a full crab meal, one of Cambodia's great culinary experiences
meals.dinner: Rusty Keyhole or Rikitikitavi restaurant in Kampot — Western-Khmer fusion with river views, mains $4–7

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island is best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Bring cash as ATMs are limited in Kep. If you prefer staying at the beach, budget bungalows on Rabbit Island are available for ~$10–15/night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot — take a slow kayak trip on the Kampot River through mangroves (~$5–8 for a 2-hour rental). Alternatively, visit the Phnom Chhnork cave temple (free entry, small tip for the local guide who holds a torch) — a stunning 7th-century brick temple inside a natural cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack up and head back to Phnom Penh by bus or shared taxi (~$7–10, 3 hours) if your departure flight is from Phnom Penh. Alternatively, buses run directly to Siem Reap from Kampot (~8 hours, $10–14) if needed. Use the remaining afternoon for last-minute souvenir shopping at the Russian Market (Phsar Tuol Tom Poung) in Phnom Penh.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Cambodia — celebrate your trip with a proper Cambodian feast. Try a set menu at a local restaurant featuring amok, lok lak, and fresh spring rolls. Reflect on the incredible history, culture, and natural beauty experienced over the past 10 days.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancake with honey and coffee at a Kampot guesthouse café — a classic Southeast Asia backpacker breakfast ($2–3)
meals.lunch: Quick roadside lunch during the return journey ($2–3)
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant or a local Phnom Penh spot for a celebratory Khmer dinner — $6–10 per person for a special final meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and allow extra time for airport transfers. Phnom Penh International Airport is about 30–45 minutes from the city center by tuk-tuk (~$7–9). Keep some USD in small bills for final tips, transport, and airport snacks. Cambodia uses both USD and Khmer Riel — change leftover Riel before departing as it's not easily exchangeable abroad.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Siem Reap Boutique Stay and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the Old Market (Psar Chas) area to get oriented. Browse local handicrafts, silk scarves, and Khmer souvenirs. Visit the nearby Preah Ang Chek Preah Ang Chorm Shrine for a gentle cultural introduction.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the famous Pub Street and Alley West for atmosphere, then enjoy a relaxed first evening in the city.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Old Market — try Amok fish curry and fresh spring rolls (mid-range, ~$8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak or Haven Restaurant — upscale Khmer cuisine with seasonal tasting menus (~$15–25 per person); great introduction to authentic Cambodian flavors

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency to Cambodian Riel (KHR) or use USD at the airport or a local bank. Tuk-tuks from the airport to the hotel cost approximately $7–10. November is the beginning of the dry season — expect pleasant, cooler weather with low humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Angkor Wat (arrive by 5:30 AM for sunrise). Watch the iconic temple reflect in the lotus pond as the sun rises over its towers — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Spend the morning exploring the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue within the Angkor Archaeological Park to Angkor Thom — visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Take a break at a nearby shaded food stall.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance over dinner at Koulen II Restaurant or Angkor Village Theatre.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or grab a baguette and coffee from a local bakery near the park entrance (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Local food stalls inside the Angkor Park serve fresh coconut, grilled corn, and noodle soups (~$3–6)
meals.dinner: Koulen II Restaurant — Apsara dance dinner show with a Khmer buffet (~$18–25 per person including the show)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass (~$62 USD) — it offers the best value for multiple temple visits. Hire a knowledgeable tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$15–20) who can navigate efficiently. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 1.5 liters of water. Modest dress required — shoulders and knees must be covered.

day_by_day.morning: Use your Angkor Pass for a second day of temple exploration. Head to Ta Prohm — the jungle temple made famous by the film Tomb Raider — where massive silk-cotton tree roots engulf ancient stone walls. Follow with Banteay Kdei and the beautiful Srah Srang reservoir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the remote and exquisite Banteay Srei Temple (~35 km northeast of Siem Reap), renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Angkor. Then stop at the Landmine Museum nearby to learn about Cambodia's tragic recent history and de-mining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the vibrant Night Market along the river for local crafts, handmade goods, and street food.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café de la Paix near the hotel (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Blue Pumpkin Café near Ta Prohm area — sandwiches, smoothies, and light bites (~$6–10)
meals.dinner: Street food tour at Siem Reap Night Market — try grilled meats, lok lak beef, and fresh fruit shakes (~$5–10 total)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is best visited in the afternoon when crowds thin slightly. The Landmine Museum (RCAF) charges a small entry fee (~$3) and is deeply moving — highly recommended for historical context. Tuk-tuk for the full day including Banteay Srei trip: ~$20–25.

day_by_day.morning: Third and final day on the Angkor Pass. Explore the lesser-visited temples of the Roluos Group — Preah Ko, Bakong, and Lolei — some of the oldest temples in the Angkor region dating to the 9th century. These are quieter and offer a more intimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for deep historical context on the Khmer Empire, its art, and its civilization. Excellent multimedia exhibits and a stunning collection of Buddha statues.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a cooking class at a local culinary school (e.g., Cooks in Tuk Tuks or Le Tigre de Papier) — learn to make Amok, green papaya salad, and banana blossom dishes.

meals.breakfast: Mahob Restaurant or local guesthouse café — rice porridge (bobor) and Khmer-style eggs (~$4–6)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near the Roluos Group — simple Khmer noodle soup and iced coffee (~$4–7)
meals.dinner: Eat your own cooking! The cooking class typically ends with a shared meal of the dishes you prepared (~$25–35 per person including class and dinner)

day_by_day.notes: The Roluos Group is about 13 km east of Siem Reap — factor in 30-minute travel time. Book the cooking class in advance online. November evenings can be slightly cool — bring a light layer for the cooking class.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day excursion to Tonlé Sap Lake — one of the largest freshwater lakes in Southeast Asia and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Board a boat to visit a floating village (Kampong Phluk or Chong Kneas) and observe the unique stilted houses, floating schools, and fishing communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop — a social enterprise training young Cambodians in traditional silk weaving, lacquerware, and stone carving. Free guided tours available and a great place to purchase authentic, ethically made souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a traditional Khmer massage at one of Siem Reap's reputable spas (e.g., Seeing Hands Massage, which employs visually impaired therapists) followed by a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Puku Café — fresh fruit bowls and pastries (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Floating village boat tour often includes or is near local eateries — fresh fish soup or grilled river fish (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant — refined Cambodian cuisine in a beautiful garden setting (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Boat tours to Tonlé Sap typically cost $15–25 per person. Go with a reputable operator to ensure the community benefits from tourism. Sunset on the lake is stunning in November. Seeing Hands Massage: ~$8–12 per hour — book ahead as it's popular.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by bus or private taxi to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by domestic flight). If traveling by bus, Giant Ibis is the most comfortable and reliable option (~$15 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh. Check in at a mid-range hotel (e.g., Plantation Hotel or Pavilion Hotel). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of Khmer royal architecture with a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles and a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with diamonds.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay (Riverside Promenade) as the sun sets over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers. Browse the lively riverside atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a bakery before departure (~$4–7)
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a rest stop along National Road 6 — local rice dishes (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant — social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including deep-fried tarantulas for the adventurous (~$12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Giant Ibis bus tickets in advance online. The Royal Palace closes at noon for a lunch break (12:00–14:00) — time your arrival accordingly. Entry fee to Royal Palace: ~$10. Phnom Penh is notably hotter and more urban than Siem Reap.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. This sobering and essential site provides profound insight into Cambodia's tragic recent history. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel 15 km south of Phnom Penh to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — a deeply moving site with an audio guide narrating personal survivor stories. Afterward, visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a striking Art Deco building with stalls selling jewelry, clothing, and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia, home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts. End the evening with a sunset cruise on the Mekong River.

meals.breakfast: Java Café near the hotel — eggs, toast, and strong Cambodian coffee (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Friends the Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a social enterprise training street youth in hospitality; excellent tapas-style Cambodian food (~$8–14)
meals.dinner: Khéma Pasteur — French-Cambodian fusion in a colonial-era villa; ideal for a special evening (~$15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — plan a quiet, reflective afternoon. Entry: Tuol Sleng ~$5, Choeung Ek ~$6 (includes audio guide). Mekong sunset cruise: ~$10–15 per person. National Museum entry: ~$10.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh by bus or shared taxi to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours), then take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem Island — one of Cambodia's most pristine and beautiful islands with turquoise waters and white sand beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem, check in at a mid-range beachfront bungalow (e.g., Lazy Beach Resort or Saracen Bay Resort). Spend the afternoon relaxing on Saracen Bay beach, swimming in crystal-clear water, and unwinding.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach with a cocktail in hand. After dark, experience the magical bioluminescent plankton that glows blue in the water when disturbed — a truly unforgettable natural phenomenon.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure or grab food at Phnom Penh bus station (~$4–6)
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or eat at a simple beachside shack on arrival (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Lazy Beach Restaurant or resort restaurant — fresh grilled seafood, coconut curry, and tropical cocktails (~$12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance through Speed Ferry Cambodia or GTVC (~$25–35 round trip). Ferries from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Samloem run several times daily. The island has limited ATMs — bring sufficient cash. Bioluminescent plankton is best viewed during new moon phases; November conditions are generally favorable.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely morning on the beach. Rent a kayak or paddleboard (~$5–10/hour) and explore the coastline. Snorkel around the coral reefs just offshore — the water clarity in November is excellent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through the island's jungle interior to the secluded M'Pai Bay village on the north side of the island — a 45-minute scenic trail offering views of both coastlines. Explore the small fishing community and its quieter beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Saracen Bay for a final beach sunset. Enjoy a bonfire dinner on the beach if your resort offers it, or dine under the stars at a beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh fruit, eggs, and coconut pancakes (~$6–9)
meals.lunch: M'Pai Bay village — simple local eateries serving fresh fish, fried rice, and cold Angkor beer (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Beachfront barbecue at your resort — whole grilled snapper, prawns, and tropical fruit platter (~$15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy sandals or light hiking shoes for the jungle trail to M'Pai Bay. Bring insect repellent. Snorkeling gear can be rented from most beach bungalows (~$5/day). The island has no cars — everything is walkable or by boat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Rong Samloem — take one last swim, collect shells, and soak in the tranquility. Pack up and take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville, then connect to Phnom Penh or Siem Reap for your departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, use any remaining time in Phnom Penh or Siem Reap to pick up last-minute souvenirs — silk products, Kampot pepper, Cambodian coffee, or handcrafted goods from Artisans Angkor.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation — final Cambodian meal, airport transfer, and farewell to Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before ferry departure (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: If transiting through Phnom Penh: Vibe Café — healthy wraps, smoothie bowls, and good WiFi (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or a final meal at a riverside restaurant near the departure city — Amok fish curry and sticky rice for a proper Cambodian farewell (~$10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Morning ferries from Koh Rong Samloem depart around 7:00–9:00 AM — confirm the schedule the night before. Allow at least 3–4 hours of buffer time between the ferry and any domestic/international flight. Domestic flights from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh or Siem Reap are available (~$50–80). Ensure your passport and travel documents are accessible. Cambodia departure tax is typically included in your ticket.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged to Siem Reap Boutique Stay with a welcome refreshment en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private check-in experience at the boutique hotel. Freshen up and enjoy a curated welcome amenity. Take a leisurely orientation stroll through the charming French Quarter and Old Market (Phsar Chas) area to acclimate to the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's terrace or rooftop bar overlooking Siem Reap. Gentle introduction to the city with a tuk-tuk ride along the illuminated Pub Street area before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel upon arrival — seasonal Khmer salads, fresh coconut, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Cambodia's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants offering modern Khmer tasting menus using local seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. November in Cambodia is the start of the cool dry season — expect pleasant temperatures around 25–30°C with low humidity. Perfect travel weather.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided sunrise visit to Angkor Wat — arrive before 05:30 to witness the iconic reflection of the temple spires in the lotus pond. Exclusive early-access entry with a specialist historian guide who narrates the 12th-century Khmer Empire's architectural genius.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Angkor Archaeological Park exploration with a private tour of Angkor Thom — the Bayon Temple (famous for its 216 serene stone faces), the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a picnic lunch prepared by the hotel in a shaded pavilion near the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a spa treatment at the in-house or partnered luxury spa — traditional Khmer massage using local herbs and oils. Dinner at a premium restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet featuring fresh tropical fruits, Khmer rice porridge (bobor), eggs to order, pastries, and Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch curated by the hotel — artisan sandwiches, Khmer spring rolls, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages served in the temple grounds
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — upscale Cambodian cuisine in an elegant garden setting, known for royal Khmer recipes and beautifully presented dishes

day_by_day.notes: Angkor Wat tickets must be purchased in advance (multi-day passes recommended). Wear light, breathable clothing and sun protection. A private air-conditioned vehicle with a dedicated driver is essential for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'jungle temple' famously left entwined with massive silk-cotton and strangler fig trees. Visit early morning to avoid crowds and experience the mystical light filtering through the canopy. Continue to Preah Khan, a sprawling temple complex with fewer tourists and remarkable bas-reliefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum for an immersive, air-conditioned deep-dive into Khmer civilization, artifacts, and the history of the Angkor Empire. Followed by a private batik or silk-weaving workshop at a local artisan cooperative to learn about Cambodia's rich textile heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an exclusive Apsara dance performance — the classical Khmer dance form listed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list — at a premium venue with a set dinner included.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh-pressed juices, Khmer crepes (banh chao), yogurt with local honey, and a full cooked selection
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mahob Restaurant — refined Cambodian cuisine emphasizing traditional recipes with a contemporary presentation, located near the Old Market
meals.dinner: Royal Apsara dinner experience at Angkor Village Resort or similar premium venue — multi-course Khmer set menu paired with the traditional dance performance

day_by_day.notes: Book the Apsara dinner performance well in advance as premium seats fill quickly. The Angkor National Museum is excellent for context after visiting the temples. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Ta Prohm's uneven terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private boat excursion on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Visit the floating villages of Kompong Phluk, where stilted wooden houses rise dramatically above the water. A private guide explains the unique ecosystem and the lives of the lake communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique — a renowned social enterprise preserving traditional Khmer craftsmanship including stone carving, lacquerware, and silk. Shop for premium, ethically made souvenirs. Relax at the hotel pool in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with a celebrated local chef — learn to prepare classic Khmer dishes such as amok (fish curry steamed in banana leaf), lok lak (Cambodian beef stir-fry), and mango salad. Enjoy the meal you've prepared as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — congee with ginger and pork, fresh fruit platters, Cambodian iced coffee, and pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch aboard the private boat or at a riverside restaurant near Tonlé Sap — fresh grilled river fish, Khmer noodle soup, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Private chef cooking class dinner — dishes prepared by you under expert guidance, served with Cambodian craft beer or wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap Lake levels are ideal in November post-rainy season — the lake is at its fullest and most impressive. Bring a light jacket for the boat ride. The cooking class is a wonderful cultural immersion activity.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' a 10th-century temple renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest examples of Khmer art. Private guided tour with an art historian to appreciate the detailed iconography and mythology depicted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Samré temple on the return journey — a lesser-visited but beautifully preserved 12th-century temple. Stop at the Landmine Museum (Cambodia Landmine Museum) for a sobering but important historical and humanitarian perspective on Cambodia's recent past.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in Siem Reap — panoramic views over the city. Leisurely evening in the boutique hotel followed by dinner at a premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict with Cambodian herbs, fresh tropical juices, local breads, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from the hotel or a stop at a high-quality local restaurant near Banteay Srei — Khmer curry, fresh rolls, and chilled drinks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sugar Palm Restaurant — a beloved Siem Reap institution offering authentic Cambodian family recipes in an elegant setting, known for its treang (Khmer curry) and beef loc lac

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is about 25 km from Siem Reap — a comfortable 40-minute private car journey. The carvings are extraordinarily detailed; a magnifying glass is sometimes used by enthusiasts. The Landmine Museum provides important context on Cambodia's history post-1975.

day_by_day.morning: Departure from Siem Reap to Sihanoukville (or Koh Rong Samloem) via private charter flight or premium domestic flight — approximately 1 hour. Transfer by private speedboat to a luxury beach resort on Koh Rong Samloem island, one of Cambodia's most pristine and beautiful islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the island resort and spend the afternoon unwinding on the powdery white-sand beach. Snorkeling excursion in the crystal-clear turquoise waters of the Gulf of Thailand — explore vibrant coral reefs and tropical marine life with private guide and premium equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside sunset cocktail hour with fresh seafood canapés. Romantic open-air dinner on the beach under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure — light continental selection with Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the island resort — fresh grilled lobster, Cambodian seafood soup, tropical salads, and coconut water served beachside
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner at the resort — whole grilled fresh fish, tiger prawns, Cambodian seafood curry, and a curated dessert selection with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time to visit Cambodia's islands — the weather is dry, clear, and comfortable. Book the private speedboat and resort well in advance. Koh Rong Samloem is less developed than Koh Rong, offering a more exclusive and tranquil experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise kayaking tour around the island's mangrove forests and hidden lagoons with a naturalist guide. Spot exotic birds, monitor lizards, and tropical flora. Return to the resort for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to a premium dive site around Koh Rong Samloem — explore underwater caves, coral gardens, and diverse marine species. Alternatively, enjoy a private sailing or catamaran charter around the island's coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent plankton night swim — a magical natural phenomenon where the ocean glows blue as you move through the water (Koh Rong Samloem is one of the best places in the world for this experience). Followed by a relaxed dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast served on the beach — fresh fruits, yogurt, pastries, eggs cooked to order, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — grilled barracuda, Cambodian-style crab, fresh green mango salad, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — Khmer seafood platter, coconut-based curries, and a curated dessert selection; light and fresh in keeping with the island setting

day_by_day.notes: The bioluminescent plankton experience is weather and tide dependent — the resort will advise on the best timing. No flash photography during the night swim to preserve the experience. Scuba diving certification is required for diving excursions; snorkeling is available for all.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning of leisure at the beach resort — read, relax in a private cabana, enjoy a beachside spa treatment (traditional Khmer massage or hot stone therapy), or take a stand-up paddleboarding lesson.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat trip to a secluded sandbar or neighboring small island for a private picnic lunch. Swim, snorkel, and sunbathe in complete seclusion. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the beach led by a private instructor. Followed by a farewell island dinner — a premium seafood barbecue feast with Cambodian spices and marinades.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — tropical smoothie bowls, avocado toast with local herbs, freshly baked pastries, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Private picnic on the sandbar — artisan wraps, chilled seafood, fresh tropical fruits, and chilled beverages prepared by the resort
meals.dinner: Premium beachside seafood barbecue — whole lobster, king prawns, fresh fish, grilled vegetables with Khmer dipping sauces, and a dessert of coconut sticky rice with mango

day_by_day.notes: This is a relaxation-focused day to recharge before returning to the mainland. The private sandbar picnic is a highlight — coordinate with the resort's concierge to arrange it. Sunset yoga is available through the resort's wellness program.

day_by_day.morning: Return by private speedboat from Koh Rong Samloem to Sihanoukville, then private transfer or short domestic flight back to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's vibrant capital city. Check in to a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh (e.g., Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex — the stunning official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring gilded spires, sacred Buddha statues, and immaculate gardens. Continue to the National Museum of Cambodia — an exquisite terracotta building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence (Chaktomuk) aboard a private luxury boat — sip champagne as the golden light reflects on the water and the city skyline glitters in the dusk. Dinner at a top Phnom Penh restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the island resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — Khmer fish amok, fresh spring rolls, and Cambodian beef salad with river views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant Phnom Penh — one of the city's most acclaimed fine-dining establishments offering French-Cambodian fusion cuisine with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Royal Palace is closed on certain public holidays — verify in advance. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) for the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda. The sunset Mekong cruise is a quintessential Phnom Penh experience — book a private charter for the most exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Meaningful cultural visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — essential for understanding Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge period (1975–1979). A private historian guide provides thoughtful, sensitive context. This is a sobering but profoundly important historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the vibrant Russian Market (Phsar Toul Tom Poung) for premium souvenir shopping — silk scarves, silver jewelry, lacquerware, and Cambodian handicrafts. Followed by a final Cambodian spa treatment at the hotel — a signature Khmer herbal compress massage to relax before the journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premium Phnom Penh restaurant celebrating 10 days of extraordinary Cambodian experiences. Private transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport for departure.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury hotel breakfast — extensive buffet with Cambodian and international options, fresh juices, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Romdeng Restaurant — a celebrated social enterprise restaurant serving traditional Cambodian cuisine in a beautiful French colonial villa, with proceeds supporting at-risk youth
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Khéma La Poste — elegant French-Cambodian brasserie in a stunning historic post office building in central Phnom Penh; signature dishes and a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visit is emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. Audio guides are available but a private historian guide adds invaluable depth. Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer well in advance. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security.

query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026
